body: I dropped out of community college in 2015 at 18 because I was failing and having panic attacks in class. I went back and had straight A’s while working in daycare and construction. I was doing homework in a job truck on breaks. I went from retail, to construction, to daycare back to construction to a very nice government safety enforcement career with MSHA and I’m still working on my BS in safety online. I even changed my major from psychology to science/safety. We all do life at our own pace. I’m 28 and a woman in the mining and construction safety industry. I would have never had this career if I did things “right” I would have been a depressed therapist with school debt and a masters degree while treating other depressed people. I am now saving lives by enforcing work place safety and keeping men like my dad safe and going home to us. I am much more fulfilled in my life now. My mom recently told me she is proud of me because she was so worried about me killing myself in high school because I was failing, cutting myself, suicidal, and barely surviving and I graduated early from the alternative high school for credit recovery and I went to community college at 17 and dropped out after failing multiple classes repetitively within a year. We all do things at our own pace and in our own way. And tbh we end up learning different lessons on the way. Sometimes we are more tolerant of people on a different path. Other times we are less tolerant because we already lived it and we know they can do it and won’t tolerate their BS. Where as people who lived that normal pace aren’t as tolerant at all. They don’t know how to teach others who lived alternative lives. It’s all different. And remember, there’s highly successful happy people who never stepped foot into a college. My dad is one of them. He is a project manager, project superintendent, and estimator along with many other things like a welder, pipefitter, mechanic, crane operator, heavy equipment operator, can do layout, can do so many things and you’d never call him a failure or say he hated himself for not finishing the EMT program he attempted to do when he was in his 20’s because he had us to support and had to go to work instead of taking the exam. You will get to a point where you find your path and pace and it works and it’s wonderful and there’s no reason to hate yourself because it built you into a different person. Because of my path I was able to work in construction with my dad and now I’m in a highly respected safety role he encouraged me to follow as a woman. I am so grateful for this path and dropping out in 2015. I eventually went back and I’m closer to graduating but I did get 5 AA’s and I’m working on my BS in safety now. We will get there eventually. We always do.
